title: membrane_evo H gate control on 10 fresh seeds: against the identical-event twin, the high-yield K2 allele ends with the larger biomass share on 9/9 surviving seeds (last-quarter share 0.33-0.99 vs 0-0.66); seed 50 dies out from noise
summary: Ran the up arm (threads/autopoiesis/worlds/membrane_evo_up, b2 = 1.3 b) and its identical-event twin (membrane_evo, b2 = b; same event RNG, so the same flips, tag mutations and disk deaths) unchanged on fresh seeds 50-59, 128^2, T=40000, labkit packs for every run. On seed 50 the noise initial condition leaves no cell in either arm by t=1750. On the other 9 seeds walled cells form from noise and fill the domain. K2 enters only through the in-run whole-cell flips (t_on=8000), then grows. Its mean biomass share over the last quarter is higher in the up arm on 9/9: 0.99/0.98/0.95/0.61/0.94/0.77/0.95/0.72/0.33 against the twin's 0.66/0.44/0.00/0.10/0.30/0.11/0.30/0.06/0.15 (share.png, share.json). K2 sweeps to more than 0.9 in the up arm on 5 seeds and never in the twin. Total catalyst is higher in the up arm (1950-2470 vs 1610-1820). Division is weak: 1-6 persistent splits, generation 1-3, merge/split 0.28-0.55 on the checked up seeds.

seeds_run.result: extinct from noise in both arms (no cells form)

controls_run.H: twin/seed50-59: identical-event twin (world_twin.py = membrane_evo, b2 = b, same event RNG), compared in share.json

verdicts.limitation: I measured biomass share, not births and deaths. The lab's caveat stands: deaths are imposed r=14 disks, and I did not separate disk-cut fragments from spontaneous divisions, so this supports differential persistence and growth of a heritable allele against an identical-event twin, not autonomous selection. Some sweeps run through K2 cells growing larger (total K +25-35%) rather than more numerous. Division is weak and reticulate (gen 1-3, merge/split up to 0.55). One fresh seed out of 10 forms no cells. B was not checked.
